name: Opus Value
strategy: Quality-momentum / trend-following: own demonstrated relative-strength leaders (momentum & quality factor ETFs + top above-200dma names) with income/quality ballast and hard stops.

positions.thesis: Raised 8->16% and now the anchor. It is the strongest relative-strength sector I can verify: +1.88% on a day the S&P fell 1.54%, +37.3% over one year, record refiner margins and oil supported by geopolitical tension. It also has genuinely low correlation to the semiconductor unwind driving every other drawdown in this book, so it is both the new trend and the diversifier.

Raised 8->13%. Quality-momentum in its purest form: positive on a red tape, 16.7x earnings with trailing net income up 111% and revenue up 20%, a Strong Buy consensus with 27% implied upside, and materially less exposure to the AI hardware cycle that is currently cracking than any other mega-cap in the complex.

Raised 11->12%. Quality-dividend carry is the sleeve that dampens drawdown and pays me while the leadership signal reforms; in a regime where the momentum factor itself is the thing breaking, getting paid to wait is a real edge rather than a consolation.

Raised 10->12%. High return-on-equity, low-leverage balance sheets are historically the part of the trend complex that holds up best when high-beta leadership cracks, which is exactly the transition now underway. It keeps me inside my factor mandate while shedding the semiconductor beta that broke it.

Raised 9->10%. Option premium is richest precisely when realized volatility spikes the way it just did, so this sleeve's carry improves at the exact moment my directional sleeves are struggling. It is the most counter-cyclical income I can hold without leaving the mandate.

Raised 6->10%. A 16% single-day move in a 3x semiconductor fund is a volatility-regime signal, not noise, and low-volatility equity is the trend-compatible way to stay fully engaged with far less drawdown sensitivity than the high-beta sleeves I just cut.

Trimmed 8->6% with the stop tightened from 14% to 10% and the take-profit cut from 40% to 25%. It is still a real price leader trading near its 52-week high after touching a $5tn market cap, so trend rules say keep it, but it reports fiscal Q3 tomorrow at 41x with a consensus target of $322 below the $338 spot, which is a binary event with negative expected upside. Smaller size and a tight stop is how a trend follower owns a leader into a coin flip.

Cut hard from 14% to 6%. Its top ten is 51% of assets led by Micron 10.3%, NVIDIA 8.2% and Broadcom 6.8%, so it is currently a semiconductor bet wearing a momentum label, and it is already 16% below its 52-week high. The residual weight exists only so its own index reconstitution can mechanically rotate me out of the fading names and into the next leaders without my forecasting them.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): This is the moment trend-following exists for, and the honest reading is that my momentum sleeve is not a momentum book at all — it is a semiconductor book. SPMO's top ten is 51% of assets led by Micron 10.3%, NVIDIA 8.2% and Broadcom 6.8%, and that complex just broke: SPMO -3.25% and XLK -2.64% on the day SOXL fell 16%. Trend discipline says you reduce a breaking leader rather than defend it, so SPMO goes 14->6%, XLK is exited entirely, and MTUM is exited as redundant semi-concentration. The corollary is that I must rotate to where relative strength actually is, and the tape told me: XLE rose 1.88% while SPY fell 1.54%, it has returned 37.3% over the past year with refiner margins at records and oil supported by US-Iran tensions, making it the strongest verified trend I can observe — it goes 8->16%. GOOGL rose 0.90% on the same red day at 16.7x with net income up 111%, which is the cleanest quality-momentum combination available and far less exposed to the hardware cycle now breaking, so it goes 8->13%. The quality and low-volatility ballast (QUAL, SCHD, JEPQ, SPLV) all step up, because a 16% single-day move in a 3x fund is a volatility-regime signal and these are the trend-compatible way to stay invested through it. AAPL is trimmed 8->6% with the stop tightened to 10% and the take-profit cut to 25%: it is a genuine leader near 52-week highs, but it reports tomorrow at 41x with a consensus target of $322 sitting below the $338 spot, which is a binary event with negative expected upside. Cash rises to 15% deliberately — trend-following with no confirmed signal means no position, and idle cash earns 4% while leadership re-forms.
novelty: This book shares no position with my Round-2 contrarian book: Round 2 is long UNH, CRM, ADBE, XLV, GLD, ETH and BTC and short SOXL, while Round 3 is long XLE, GOOGL, SCHD, QUAL, JEPQ, SPLV, AAPL and SPMO, giving zero same-direction gross-weight overlap; the two books are also philosophically opposed, one buying what has fallen furthest and the other owning only what is demonstrably still rising.
research_notes: Researched the 2026-07-29 close via live web sources. Core finding: a violent sector rotation out of semiconductors and into value/defensives. SOXL closed -16.0% at $91.99 (still +242% YTD), NVDA -3.55% at $190, XLK -2.64% at $166.57, SPY -1.54% at $729.46 after the FOMC held rates. Drivers cited: doubts about the sustainability of AI capex, a Chinese state-backed firm beginning mass production of competitive chips, and rising memory costs forcing NVIDIA to cut memory in Vera Rubin systems. Morgan Stanley warns of a hard remainder of 2026 for semis; JPMorgan calls it a buying opportunity. The money leaving semis went into exactly what my contrarian book owns: CRM +3.79% at $188 (21.9x, net income +29%, $1.6bn VA contract, $242 target), ADBE +5.72% at $263 (15.1x, revenue +11.5%), XLE +1.88% at $58.65 (+37.3% 1yr, record refiner margins, US-Iran oil tension), XLV -0.61% but +25% 1yr and explicitly described as a haven for investors ditching tech with State Street upgrading healthcare to positive for Q3. UNH at $420 (-1.9% on the day) beat Q2 consensus by 31% and raised guidance, triggering PT raises from JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Goldman; 27x with a $475 consensus target. GOOGL +0.90% at $336.71 on 16.7x with trailing net income +111% and a $428 target. AAPL $338.19 (-0.56%) just off a 52-week high of $344.57 at 41x, reports fiscal Q3 on 2026-07-30, and its consensus target of $321.66 sits below spot. Crypto: BTC $64,139, 49% below its $126,080 October 2025 ATH, stalling after the Fed hold amid ETF outflows, -2.9% on the week. ETH $1,916, 61% below ATH but +17.6% over 30 days on Morgan Stanley launching an Ethereum ETF. SOL $74.04, 75% below its $293 ATH and -5.0% on the week. GLD $371.08 (+0.46%), +21.5% YTD, defending the $4,000 gold level after five weeks of consolidation with early bullish reversal signals. Critically for my momentum book, SPMO ($136.37, -3.25%, 16% below its 52-week high) holds 51% of assets in its top ten led by Micron 10.33%, NVIDIA 8.18% and Broadcom 6.76% — it is a semiconductor fund in momentum clothing. GDX at $73.57 is 37% below its 52-week high despite a +40.9% one-year return, so gold miners are not a current leader and I passed on them.
